purpose: Small cross-runtime semantic fixtures for Run, Observation, Verification, Evidence, authority, continuation, and cache boundaries. These fixtures do not prove runtime conformance until executed by at least two materially different implementations.

cases.name: run identity is stable
assertions: run_id remains identical across continuation and observation records
the same run_id is not silently reused for a different goal

cases.name: observation is not evidence
assertions: an observation may be recorded without automatically becoming evidence
an evidence reference carries attributable source identity
evidence status does not imply truth without verification

cases.name: verification may reject a result
assertions: verification status may be failed even when execution produced a result
a failed verification cannot be upgraded to passed by repetition alone

cases.name: ambiguous external effect remains unknown
assertions: UNKNOWN_OUTCOME is not treated as success
UNKNOWN_OUTCOME is not treated as safe-to-repeat
reconciliation is required before authoritative terminal classification

cases.name: authority is scoped and pinned
assertions: authority is bound to an explicit concern
repository identity and exact ref are preserved
known gaps remain visible
protocol reachability does not itself establish semantic authority

cases.name: continuation frontier is a projection
assertions: frontier revisions are ordered
frontier records may identify open items and next actions
frontier state does not itself authorize an effect

cases.name: cache is a valuable reusable artifact without authority
assertions: a cache remains identifiable as a reusable artifact after creation
cache reuse policy is explicit and may require revalidation
stale or invalid cache state does not require silent deletion
cache reuse does not establish evidence, truth, authorization, or semantic authority
